title: Getting Started with ROvis
text: First, need load required packages. Second, generate simulated data mimics structure COVID-19 test data. use data January 2022 example graphs. first 5 rows look like :
code: library(tidyverse) library(ROvis.utils) library(ROvis.ggplot2) # nolint: missing_package_linter. # Set seed for reproducibility set.seed(123)  # Generate data for multiple regions used in the examples dat_test_cov <- expand_grid(   Date_of_statistics = seq(as_date("2022-01-01"), as_date("2022-01-31"), by = "day"),   Security_region_name = c(     "Brabant-Noord", "Brabant-Zuidoost", "Midden- en West-Brabant",     "Noord- en Oost-Gelderland", "Gelderland-Midden", "Gelderland-Zuid", "Onbekend"   ) ) |>   mutate(     # Calculate day number (1-31) for upward trend     day_num = as.numeric(Date_of_statistics - as_date("2022-01-01")) + 1,     # Generate test numbers with slight variation     Tested_with_result = as.integer(round(rnorm(n(), mean = 1800, sd = 50))),     # Positive tests with steep upward trend: start at ~15% and increase to ~50%     positive_rate = 0.15 + (day_num - 1) * (0.50 - 0.15) / 30,     Tested_positive = as.integer(round(       Tested_with_result * positive_rate * rnorm(n(), mean = 1, sd = 0.05)     ))   ) |>   select(Date_of_statistics, Security_region_name, Tested_positive) |>   mutate(Security_region_name = factor(Security_region_name)) |>   as_tibble() dat_test_cov |>   head(5) ## # A tibble: 5 × 3 ##   Date_of_statistics Security_region_name      Tested_positive ##   <date>             <fct>                               <int> ## 1 2022-01-01         Brabant-Noord                         256 ## 2 2022-01-01         Brabant-Zuidoost                      252 ## 3 2022-01-01         Midden- en West-Brabant               264 ## 4 2022-01-01         Noord- en Oost-Gelderland             263 ## 5 2022-01-01         Gelderland-Midden                     279

title: Getting Started with ROvis
text: explore RIVM color palettes included ROvis, run ro_show_colors() R Console. open visual display color palettes Viewer pane, can also hover color see corresponding hex code. default 18 RIVM colors shown. standardized colors recommended use visualizations maintain consistency across reports. colors also lighter (’_tint90’) darker (’_tint110’) variations. shades helpful need use several colors together, maintain similar contrast levels. need multiple colors, can use one predefined color palettes. standardized reporting, recommend using built-categorical gender palettes instead creating custom palettes. can see demonstration available palettes : demonstrate use colors, select security regions “Brabant” using filter. start creating plot without specifying colors. Thus, resulting plot shows standard colors ggplot.  Now, want apply RIVM colors using ROvis.utils::ro_color() part scale_colour_manual(). categorical data, use standard RIVM categorical color palette. recommended order palette followed, starting ‘hemelblauw’ first category.  Alternatively, can use ROvis.utils::ro_color_categorical() function scale_colour_manual(). function returns hex codes categorical color palette correct order, makes easy use.  want learn using color palettes ordinal continuous data, go Working color palettes vignette.
code: ro_show_colors() ro_show_colors(palette_name = "categorical") ro_show_colors(palette_name = "gender_con") ro_show_colors(palette_name = "gender_unc") ro_show_colors(palette_name = "greys") fig_brab <- dat_test_cov |>   filter(     Security_region_name %in% c("Midden- en West-Brabant", "Brabant-Noord", "Brabant-Zuidoost")   ) |>   ggplot(aes(     x = Date_of_statistics,     y = Tested_positive,     color = Security_region_name   )) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_point() fig_brab fig_brab +   scale_colour_manual(     values = c(       "Brabant-Noord" = ro_color("hemelblauw"),       "Brabant-Zuidoost" = ro_color("donkergeel"),       "Midden- en West-Brabant" = ro_color("robijnrood")     )   ) fig_brab +   scale_color_manual(values = c(ROvis.utils::ro_color_categorical()))

title: ggplot2 in RO style
text: use small synthetic dataset demonstration purposes:
code: library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) library(ROvis.utils) # nolint: missing_package_linter. library(ROvis.ggplot2) # nolint: missing_package_linter. sex_levels <- c("Women", "Men", "Total")  # Reported cases per age group and sex dat_cases <- data.frame(   agegroup = rep(c("0-19", "20-39", "40-59", "60-79", "80+"), times = 3),   sex = factor(rep(sex_levels, each = 5), levels = sex_levels),   n = c(     12000,     48000,     61000,     43000,     18000,     10000,     45000,     58000,     39000,     14000,     22000,     93000,     119000,     82000,     32000   ) )  # Reported cases per week (three series) dat_weekly <- data.frame(   week = factor(rep(1:12, times = 3), levels = 1:12),   sex = factor(rep(sex_levels, each = 12), levels = sex_levels),   n = c(     800,     950,     1100,     1400,     1600,     1550,     1300,     1100,     900,     750,     600,     500,     700,     880,     1020,     1300,     1480,     1420,     1180,     990,     820,     680,     540,     440,     1500,     1830,     2120,     2700,     3080,     2970,     2480,     2090,     1720,     1430,     1140,     940   ) )  # Reported cases per day of the week dat_weekday <- data.frame(   day = factor(     c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"),     levels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")   ),   n = c(180, 165, 172, 190, 210, 95, 60) )

title: ggplot2 in RO style
text: ro_gg_plot designed complete add-ggplot2 graphs. ’s theme. applies lower-level theme (ro_gg_theme), makes adjustments top . Unlike ro_gg_theme(), returns theme() object add + anywhere chain, ro_gg_plot() needs see whole plot (data, geoms, scales) decide add. takes complete ggplot2 object input returns modified one. Build plot fully first, save object, call ro_gg_plot() object last step:  note piping: pipe straight + chain ro_gg_plot(), |> binds tighter +. Writing applies ro_gg_plot() result labs(...), whole plot (error, since ’s ggplot object). Always assign finished plot variable first!
code: p_basic <- dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   ggplot(aes(x = agegroup, y = n)) +   geom_col(fill = ro_color("hemelblauw")) +   labs(     title = "Cases by age group",     subtitle = "Women only",     x = "Age class",     y = "Value"   )  ro_gg_plot(p_basic) Keep in mind that when using ro_gg_theme, you need to take additional coding steps to fully comply     with the RIVM style. For more information, see the ROvis documentation website:     https://rivm-syso.github.io/ROvis This message is displayed once per session. ggplot(...) +   geom_col() +   labs(...) |>   ro_gg_plot()

title: ggplot2 in RO style
text: Notice set fill = "Sex" labs(), legend title shown: RO style never displays one, ro_gg_plot() removes automatically. ro_gg_plot() also fixes bar/column styling match RO style: group bars occupies 80% category slot (remaining 20% gap groups), bars within group sit flush gap, bars get outline. x-axis ticks moved category boundary groups — ’s small tick marks can see “0-19”/“20-39”/“40-59” , instead one centered category. discrete x-axis works :  group ticks sit boundary day, age-group chart . horizontal bar chart, swap x y aes() set flip = TRUE:   ro_gg_plot() detects bar/column chart, leaves ggplot2’s default axis expansion limits alone (line chart usually shouldn’t touch x-axis way bar chart ): adds thousands separator y-axis labels still removes legend title relocates y-axis title.
code: p_grouped <- dat_cases |>   filter(sex != "Total") |>   ggplot(aes(x = agegroup, y = n, fill = sex)) +   geom_col(position = "dodge") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c(Women = ro_color("robijnrood"), Men = ro_color("hemelblauw"))   ) +   labs(     title = "Cases by age group and sex",     x = "Age class",     y = "Value",     fill = "Sex"   )  ro_gg_plot(p_grouped) p_weekday <- dat_weekday |>   ggplot(aes(x = day, y = n)) +   geom_col(fill = ro_color("hemelblauw")) +   labs(     title = "Cases by day of the week",     x = "Day",     y = "Value"   )  ro_gg_plot(p_weekday) p_horizontal <- dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   ggplot(aes(x = n, y = agegroup)) +   geom_col(fill = ro_color("hemelblauw")) +   labs(     title = "Cases by age group",     subtitle = "Women only",     x = "Value",     y = "Age class"   )  ro_gg_plot(p_horizontal, flip = TRUE) p_line <- dat_weekly |>   filter(sex != "Total") |>   ggplot(aes(x = week, y = n, color = sex, group = sex)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   scale_color_manual(     values = c(Women = ro_color("robijnrood"), Men = ro_color("hemelblauw"))   ) +   labs(     title = "Weekly cases by sex",     x = "Week",     y = "Value",     color = "Sex"   )  ro_gg_plot(p_line)

title: Apply the RO ggplot2 theme and auto-fix common RO style requirements — ro_gg_plot
text: Applies ro_gg_theme() cosmetic theme. Removes legend titles (RO style never shows one), fill, colour/color, shape, linetype, alpha, size. bar/column charts (layer using geom_col()/geom_bar()), sets group width 80% category slot, removes padding bars within group (switching position_dodge2() position_dodge() needed), removes bar outlines. Tick marks moved category boundary groups via ro_gg_group_ticks(). Works default flipped (flip = TRUE) orientation. bar/column line charts (layer using geom_col()/geom_bar()/geom_line()), user already added scale continuous axis, applies ro_gg_remove_axis_gap() expansion, ro_gg_axis() axis limits (continuous axis starts 0), thousands separator labels. chart types (e.g. scatter plots) get thousands separator. Relocates y-axis title RO position via ro_gg_y_title(), y-axis title present. Works default flipped (flip = TRUE) orientation.

(2) fully replacing 'existing theme %+replace% theme()'. ro_gg_theme(), chose first approach ('existing theme + theme(...)').method offers greater flexibility users, making easier apply additional customization top ro_gg_theme() defaults.

title: Relocate y-axis title of ggplot object to RIVM style position — ro_gg_y_title
text: Relocates y-axis title existing ggplot object (theme_ggrivm(version = "1.0") applied) right location, following RIVM design guidelines. function calculates y-coordinate highest grid line positions y-axis title slightly value optimal appearance. Note: Since title may (partly) fall outside plot area, always use function combination ggplot's coord_cartesian(clip = ""). Please note: experimental function. features behavior may change future updates.
